newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says no talks until miners leave Bonn.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says no talks until miners leave Bonn.

text.p: The German government, under siege by thousands of angry miners, insisted on Thursday that protesting pitworkers must leave the capital before talks on planned subsidy cuts could be resumed.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl postponed a meeting with Miners union leader Hans Berger on Tuesday after thousands of angry miners converged on Bonn, creating what Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl called an atmosphere of blackmail.

Both Bohl and Berger said their sides stuck to their positions. Bohl said Bonn wanted to slash its 10 billion mark annual subsidies for the overpriced coal sector to 3.9 billion marks ($2.2 billion) by the year 2005.
The IGBE miners union, which accuses the government of breaking a pledge to phase out the aid gradually, was ready to see the subsidies drop only to 6.5 billion marks.
Berger, already under pressure from his rank and file for being too flexible in earlier talks with Kohl, said he would ask the miners at a rally later on Tuesday to return home.

"We'll have a rally this afternoon and tell our colleagues the condition for further talks is that they leave Bonn," he said. "I'll urge them to do that and see what happens. But without meeting this condition there will be no talks."
Berger was not sure the miners would heed his pleas. If they did and he then failed to reach an acceptable compromise on Thursday, he said, "the miners will come back in droves."
